findings.title: Incorrect filtering of constraints in CreateTableOp
findings.explanation: The logic in `alembic/operations/schemaobj.py` incorrectly filters out all constraints that are type-bound, even if they are not the ones that should be skipped. The condition `isinstance(elem, Index) or (isinstance(elem, Constraint) and sqla_compat._is_type_bound(elem))` effectively excludes all constraints that are type-bound from the `constraints` list, which causes many other constraints (like ForeignKeyConstraint, UniqueConstraint, etc.) to be missing from the generated `create_table` statement, leading to test failures. The intention was likely to only skip the specific type-bound CHECK constraint, not all constraints.
findings.evidence:
if isinstance(elem, Index)
            or (
                isinstance(elem, Constraint)
                # a type-bound constraint, e.g. the CHECK constraint
                # generated by Boolean / Enum, was already produced again
                # by the column's type when the column was added to the
                # Table above, so skip it here so that it isn't doubled.
                # SQLAlchemy to_metadata() skips these in the same way
                and sqla_compat._is_type_bound(elem)
            )
